en.title: Daenerys Targaryen Officially Returns to Game of Thrones in 2027
en.summary: Seven years after her controversial departure from the screen, Daenerys Targaryen is set to make a significant return to the Game of Thrones universe. The Dragon Queen will feature in a major new video game, alongside other beloved characters.
en.body:
The realm of Westeros is expanding once again, and this time, a familiar face is making a comeback. Daenerys Targaryen, the Mother of Dragons herself, is officially set to return in the upcoming video game **Game of Thrones: War for Westeros**, scheduled for an early 2027 release. This marks a significant revival for a character whose fate in the original series remains a potent topic of discussion among fans, seven years after her on-screen conclusion.

**Game of Thrones: War for Westeros** promises to immerse players in the epic struggles of Westeros, featuring iconic characters such as Jon Snow and Jaime Lannister alongside Daenerys. Players will have the opportunity to command various forces, including the formidable dragons that became synonymous with the Targaryen dynasty. Originally slated for a 2026 launch, the game experienced a delay, but the confirmation of Daenerys's inclusion is sure to reignite excitement. Beyond this major title, the Dragon Queen is also making an appearance in the free-to-play mobile strategy game **Game of Thrones: Legends**. From November 5th to November 9th, players of **Legends** can experience a new event titled "Robb's War," which will feature Daenerys as part of its content, offering a more accessible, albeit temporary, way to interact with the character.

## A Dragon's Second Coming

The return of **Daenerys Targaryen** is more than just a character cameo; it’s a strategic move by the **Game of Thrones** franchise to leverage its most impactful figures. While the original series finale left many fans divided, the enduring popularity of characters like Daenerys, Jon Snow, and Tyrion Lannister continues to be a driving force for new content. The inclusion of Daenerys in **War for Westeros**, a title that sounds like it will delve deep into large-scale conflict, suggests an opportunity to explore her narrative from different perspectives or within new scenarios. The earlier spin-off series, **A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms**, and the ongoing **House of the Dragon**, demonstrate HBO's commitment to expanding the universe, and bringing back such a pivotal character in a major gaming release solidifies the interconnectedness of these ventures. It offers a chance for fans to perhaps experience a Westeros where key events unfold differently, or to simply relive the power and presence of one of the saga's most complex protagonists.

## What Fans Can Expect

This dual return—in a major console/PC title and a mobile game—shows a broad approach to engaging the **Game of Thrones** fanbase. For those eagerly awaiting **War for Westeros**, the early 2027 release date is now a key date to circle. The anticipation for this game is palpable, especially with the promise of controlling dragons and interacting with a roster of legendary characters. Meanwhile, the limited-time event in **Game of Thrones: Legends** provides a taste of what's to come, allowing mobile gamers to get their fix of Westerosi conflict and strategy. The franchise is clearly betting on the enduring appeal of its core characters and the rich lore of George R.R. Martin's world to captivate audiences across different platforms and playstyles.

## What's Next

**Game of Thrones: War for Westeros** is slated for an early 2027 release. The "Robb's War" event in **Game of Thrones: Legends** runs from November 5th to November 9th. Further details regarding **War for Westeros** and its specific features are expected to be announced in the coming months.

content_raw: 2026 has been a huge year for Game of Thrones fans, who were treated to not only one, but two new seasons of spin-off shows. Back in January, almost one full year ago, Game of Thrones fans flocked to the first season of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms , which spent months in the top 10 on HBO Max. The show was renewed for Season 2 long before the Season 1 premiere, and it’s confirmed to return for its second season in the first half of 2026. Additionally, HBO also released the third season of House of the Dragon over the summer, which mostly won back fans after a divisive second season. The streamer has already confirmed that the show will end with its fourth season, which is expected to film in 2027 and be released in 2028.
